# CUI // SP-CTI
#
# floci RUNTIME BASE IMAGES -- the images floci pulls at run time for its
# container-backed services (flx-airgap-02). Distinct from `images-floci.txt`,
# which pins the emulator's OWN image: having floci cached is necessary and NOT
# sufficient, because none of these ship inside it.
#
# Bundle them for the high side with:
#     python tools/airgap/image_vendor.py --save --topic floci-runtime --json
#
# EVERY DIGEST HERE WAS MEASURED, not read off a README: `docker events
# --filter type=image` recorded while a live floci 2.0.1 was driven through
# each container-backed service with boto3. Method, dates and the per-service
# attribution are in args/floci_runtime_images.yaml, which is the declaration
# of record -- `tests/cloud/test_floci_runtime_images.py` asserts the two agree,
# so ONE measured fact cannot come to be spelled two ways.
#
# VENDOR THE VARIANTS YOU DECLARE. Lambda needs one image PER RUNTIME and RDS
# one PER ENGINE, so this file is the full measured set and not a shopping list:
# a deployment running only a python Lambda over postgres needs four of these
# eleven. `python -m tools.cloud.runtime_images --check --services lambda,rds
# --variants python3.11,postgres` says which.

# lambda/python3.11 -- public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.11
public.ecr.aws/lambda/python@sha256:755093e1da2ba33f6bd2295c5a6a7ed8b94f1ef347b6ca649874d9cbef5a3e3c

# lambda/nodejs20.x -- public.ecr.aws/lambda/nodejs:20
public.ecr.aws/lambda/nodejs@sha256:a4440274d6f0fb4e6cb92cd5f2a97254efe6612f631d9974b197ecbd4a61fcab

# rds/postgres -- postgres:16.3-alpine
#   The tag is floci's DEFAULT EngineVersion: the ref is built as
#   `postgres:<EngineVersion>-alpine` (measured 2026-09-12). A NEWER postgres is
#   NOT an upgrade for this line -- vendoring 18.6-alpine instead of this one
#   leaves the default path unvendored. See
#   docs/audits/artifact-fresh-5b1750f240-rds-postgres-pin.md.
postgres@sha256:36ed71227ae36305d26382657c0b96cbaf298427b3f1eaeb10d77a6dea3eec41

# rds/mysql -- mysql:8.0.36
#   The tag is floci's DEFAULT EngineVersion: the ref is built as
#   `mysql:<EngineVersion>` -- NO suffix, unlike the postgres line above
#   (measured 2026-09-12). A NEWER mysql is NOT an upgrade for this line, and
#   `Engine=mariadb` is a different repository entirely. See
#   docs/audits/artifact-fresh-da63da118f-rds-mysql-pin.md.
mysql@sha256:a532724022429812ec797c285c1b540a644c15e248579c6bfdf12a8fbaab4964

# elasticache/redis -- valkey/valkey:8
#   The tag is a CONSTANT inside floci 2.0.1, not a version this tree chose:
#   the native binary contains exactly one valkey image string and
#   EngineVersion is ignored (measured 2026-09-12 -- default, 7.1, 99.99 and
#   Engine=valkey/EngineVersion=9 ALL started valkey/valkey:8). valkey 9 exists
#   upstream and floci cannot be made to request it, so vendoring 9 instead of
#   this line leaves EVERY ElastiCache path unvendored. DIGEST RE-MEASURED the
#   same day: the tag moved off sha256:98c6217c... to the digest below, same
#   engine (Valkey 8.1.10) either side -- a base-image rebuild, not an upgrade.
#   See docs/audits/artifact-fresh-ee3339893b-elasticache-valkey-pin.md.
valkey/valkey@sha256:3fbd2e3e4b6e85e046c1e7c215e8f79087bc0357789184305806664e320996f3

# elasticache/memcached -- memcached:1.6
memcached@sha256:75c93cc91e76853da7c029e74d6e8dbd44774dd3713c93be8cd1971ad26120a4

# opensearch -- opensearchproject/opensearch:2.19.5
opensearchproject/opensearch@sha256:4ee82ecb35d837a6186c81aaa64c8a5bce71aa956edbd87f1f684ab56af52c44

# kafka -- redpandadata/redpanda:latest   # MUTABLE TAG upstream -- re-measure, never assume
redpandadata/redpanda@sha256:468bd13a9f2bd24794cb7fddc867c767fb1008b9a07b297b89fde48c564d7d96

# ec2 -- public.ecr.aws/amazonlinux/amazonlinux:2023   # ROLLING TAG upstream -- re-measure, never assume
#   The tag is floci's OWN default: `defaultDockerImage` in its embedded AMI
#   catalogue, which an unknown ImageId falls back to (measured 2026-09-12).
#   Amazon Linux 2027 exists upstream and floci 2.0.1 cannot request it. But
#   `2023` is a MAJOR-VERSION tag that upstream REBUILDS, so the digest moves
#   without the tag moving: re-measured 2026-09-12 from AL 2023.12.20260831
#   (sha256:fb70bd54...) to AL 2023.12.20260909 below. See
#   docs/audits/artifact-fresh-b5394142b3-ec2-amazonlinux-pin.md.
public.ecr.aws/amazonlinux/amazonlinux@sha256:a0646b8bd35abf5ca3ab94d8cdb5691b9024e19c357531eeefd0ac4762836438

# eks -- rancher/k3s:latest   # MUTABLE TAG upstream -- re-measure, never assume
rancher/k3s@sha256:5e0707cfd1239b358ef73f3254bc3eadc027dd30cd5ec6ca41e29e47652a1b8c

# ecr -- registry:2
registry@sha256:a3d8aaa63ed8681a604f1dea0aa03f100d5895b6a58ace528858a7b332415373
